      3.   Zoning ordinance map amendment applications shall be submitted to
the Director.
   C.   Completeness: See Section
8-6-5.
   D.   Notice: See Section
8-6-8.
   E.   Decision:
      1.   Staff Review: The Director shall review the application and prepare
and send a recommendation for the Commission's review.
      2.   Commission Review: The Commission shall review the application and
submit its recommendation to the Board:
         a.   To approve the zoning ordinance map amendment;
         b.   To deny the zoning ordinance map amendment; or
         c.   To approve the zoning ordinance map amendment with suggested
changes.
      3.   Board Decision: The Board shall make the final decision:
         a.   To approve the zoning ordinance map amendment;
         b.   To deny the zoning ordinance map amendment; or
         c.   To approve the zoning ordinance map amendment with changes.
   F.   Required Findings: To grant a zoning ordinance map amendment, the
following findings must be made:
      1.   The zoning ordinance map amendment conforms with the applicable
comprehensive plan;
      2.   The zoning ordinance map amendment complies with the regulations
outlined for the proposed base district, specifically the purpose statement;
      3.   The subject property shall meet the minimum dimensional standards of
the proposed zoning district;
      4.   The zoning ordinance map amendment shall not cause detriment to
public health, safety, and welfare;
      5.   The zoning ordinance map amendment shall not result in demonstrable
adverse impacts upon the delivery of services by any political subdivision
providing public services within the planning jurisdiction including school
districts; and
      6.   For zoning ordinance map amendments within a planned community (PC)
base district, the amendment complies with the planned community implementation
plan.
   G.   Appeals: See Section
8-6-13.
   H.   Scope Of Approval: The approval of a zoning ordinance map amendment
does not authorize the development of land. A zoning ordinance map amendment
allows property owners to apply for permits or actions that are consistent with
the zoning district's standards and requirements.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-6-34: ZONING ORDINANCE TEXT AMENDMENT:
   A.   Applicability: This Section applies to any application to amend the
text of the Zoning Ordinance.
   B.   Initiation:
      1.   The Board may propose to amend the zoning ordinance text following
notice, neighborhood meeting, and public hearing procedures in Sections
8-6-4,
8-6-8, and
8-6-9.
      2.   Any property owner may propose a zoning ordinance text amendment to
the Board.
      3.   Zoning ordinance text amendment applications shall be submitted to
the Director.
   C.   Completeness: See Section
8-6-5.
   D.   Notice: See Section
8-6-8.
   E.   Decision:
      1.   Staff Review: The Director shall review the application and prepare
and send a recommendation for the Commission's review.
      2.   Commission Review: The Commission shall review the application and
submit its recommendation to the Board:
         a.   To approve the zoning ordinance text amendment;
         b.   To deny the zoning ordinance text amendment; or
         c.   To approve the zoning ordinance text amendment with suggested
changes.
      3.   Board Decision: The Board shall make the final decision:
         a.   To approve the zoning ordinance text amendment;
         b.   To deny the zoning ordinance text amendment; or
         c.   To approve the zoning ordinance text amendment with changes,
subject to public notification of the changes per Section
8-6-8.
   F.   Required Findings: The Board shall make following findings to grant a
zoning ordinance text amendment:
      1.   The zoning ordinance text amendment conforms with the applicable
comprehensive plan;
      2.   The zoning ordinance text amendment is not detrimental to public
health, safety, and welfare; and
      3.   For zoning ordinance text amendments within a planned community (PC)
base district, the amendment complies with the planned community implementation
plan.
   G.   Appeals: See Section
8-6-13.
   H.   Scope Of Approval: The approval of a zoning ordinance text amendment
does not directly authorize the development of land. A zoning ordinance text
amendment simply changes the Zoning Ordinance regulations.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
CHAPTER 7
NONCONFORMITIES
SECTION:
8-7-1: Purpose And Applicability
8-7-2: Nonconforming Uses
8-7-3: Nonconforming Structures
8-7-4: Nonconforming Properties
8-7-5: Nonconforming Signs
8-7-1: PURPOSE AND APPLICABILITY:
   A.   Purpose: This Chapter governs uses, structures, properties, and other
situations that legally came into existence prior to the effective date of this
Zoning Ordinance or the effective date of future amendments to this Zoning
Ordinance, but do not comply with or conform to one or more requirements of
this Zoning Ordinance. Those situations are collectively referred to as
"nonconformities." Also, this Chapter allows any nonconforming property, use,
or structure that was lawfully existing prior to the effective date of this
Title to continue until they are removed, but not to encourage their
continuation. Nonconformities shall not expand or extend the nonconforming
aspect of the property, use, or structure, unless approved subject to the
regulations of Chapter 8-6.
   B.   Applicability: These regulations apply to any lawfully existing
nonconforming property, use, or structure in Ada County. However, a property,
use, or structure that was deemed nonconforming under past zoning regulations
but now complies with this Title is deemed conforming.
   C.   Deemed Conforming Property:
      1.   Applicability: These regulations apply to properties that:
         a.   Were not created in accord with the regulations of this Title (an
illegal division of property);
         b.   That were of record in the Ada County recorder's office prior to
January 1, 1985; and
         c.   Have not changed their boundaries except by governmental action
as specified in subsection
8-7-4B.
      2.   Current Dimensional Standards: A deemed conforming property is
eligible for building permits if it meets the dimensional standards for the
base district in which it is now located.
      3.   Former Dimensional Standards Or Dwelling Constructed: A deemed
conforming property is eligible for building permits if it meets one of the
following standards:
         a.   The property met the dimensional standards for the applicable
base district at the time it was created; or
         b.   A dwelling was constructed or placed on the property prior to
January 1, 1985. However, if the dwelling is subsequently damaged or destroyed
by fire, flood, explosion, wind, earthquake, war, riot, calamity or other
catastrophic event after January 1, 1985, the property remains eligible for a
building permit.
   D.   Dwellings, Two Or More Existing:
      1.   Any property that has two (2) or more existing dwellings that were
built prior to May 20, 1968, or were principal permitted dwellings approved in
accordance with the zoning regulations that were in effect at the time those
dwellings were built, is deemed a nonconforming use.
      2.   Each dwelling is subject to the standards in Section
8-7-2 below.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-7-2: NONCONFORMING USES:
   A.   Generally: The nonconforming use may continue if the use remains lawful
and the use is not expanded or extended, unless approved subject to the
regulations of Chapter 8-6.
   B.   Definition: For the purposes of this Section, the term "expanded or
extended" includes:
      1.   Increased hours;
      2.   Increased services or programs;
      3.   Increased number of residential dwellings;
      4.   Interior renovations or structural additions that increase the
occupant load of the structure dedicated to the nonconforming use (see the Ada
County Building Code);
      5.   Any new structures accessory to the nonconforming use;
      6.   Expansion or replacement of the structure (or portions thereof)
dedicated to the nonconforming use;
      7.   Anything beyond regular maintenance and minor repairs (as required
by the Ada County Building Code); or
      8.   Any action that extends the duration or intensity of the
nonconforming use.
   C.   Abandonment: A nonconforming use that ceases for ten (10) years or is
replaced with a conforming use is deemed abandoned and shall not be
reestablished. If nonuse or vacancy continues for at least one (1) year, the
County may request resolution of the nonconforming use right according to
procedures outlined in Idaho Code Section 67-6538(2).
   D.   Damage:
      1.   A nonconforming use or structure housing a nonconforming use that is
damaged by more than fifty percent (50%) of its current assessed taxable value
by fire, flood, explosion, wind, earthquake, war, riot, calamity, or other
catastrophic event shall comply with this Title upon reconstruction.
      2.   If the damage to the nonconforming use or structure housing the
nonconforming use is fifty percent (50%) or less of the current assessed
taxable value, the nonconforming use may continue if construction or use
commences within ten (10) years of the event.
      3.   If nonuse or vacancy continues for at least one year, the County may
request resolution of the nonconforming use right according to procedures
outlined in Idaho Code Section 67-6538(2).
   E.   Exemption: Uses housed within structures listed on the national
register of historic places are exempt from this Section.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-7-3: NONCONFORMING STRUCTURES:
   A.   Generally: Nonconforming structures may be enlarged or modified if the
additions or modifications to the structure conform to this Title.
   B.   Damage:
      1.   A nonconforming structure that is damaged more than seventy-five
percent (75%) of its current assessed taxable value by fire, flood, explosion,
wind, earthquake, war, riot, calamity, or other catastrophic event, shall
comply with this Title upon restoration or reconstruction.
      2.   If the damage to the nonconforming structure is seventy-five percent
(75%) or less of the current assessed taxable value, the structure may be
restored or reconstructed if the restoration or reconstruction commences within
twelve (12) months of the event.
   C.   Exemption: Structures listed on the national register of historic
places are exempt from this Section.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-7-4: NONCONFORMING PROPERTIES:
   A.   Generally: A nonconforming property shall not be diminished in size.
   B.   Reduction By Governmental Action: Any property reduced by governmental
action that reduces an existing conforming parcel below the required lot size
is deemed a conforming property for the purpose of development. To be deemed a
conforming property, the following shall be submitted to the Development
Services Department:
      1.   Documentation the property followed the minimum property size
requirement of the applicable zoning district prior to the decrease in property
size; and
      2.   Documentation the decrease in property size was caused by
acquisition through prescription, purchase, or other means by Ada County, a
municipality within Ada County, the Ada County Highway District, Idaho
Transportation Department, utility company or corporation under the
jurisdiction of the Idaho Public Utilities Commission, or other local, state,
or federal agency.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-7-5: NONCONFORMING SIGNS:
   Nonconforming signs are deemed a nonconforming use and/or structure (as
applicable) and may continue subject to the standards established in this
Chapter.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
CHAPTER 8
ENFORCEMENT
SECTION:
8-8-1: Generally
8-8-2: Violations
8-8-3: Remedies
8-8-1: GENERALLY:
   A.   Purpose: This Chapter provides measures to enforce Zoning Ordinance
violations pursuant to Idaho Code Section 67-6527 or any other applicable
authority.
   B.   Applicability: This Chapter establishes:
      1.   Procedures through which the County seeks to ensure compliance with
the provisions of this Zoning Ordinance and obtain corrections for violations.
      2.   The remedies and penalties that apply to Zoning Ordinance
violations.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-8-2: VIOLATIONS:
   A.   Authority: Idaho Code 67-6527 provides for enforcement of ordinances
and regulations.
   B.   Generally:
      1.   Conviction of a violation of this ordinance and regulations is a
misdemeanor.
      2.   Each day that work continues after a violation notification is a
separate offense.
      3.   Violations are punishable as provided in Idaho Code Section 18-113.
      4.   A violation may be pursued through a civil action.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-8-3: REMEDIES:
   A.   Violation Of Conditions Of Approval:
      1.   This subsection applies to noncompliance with any conditions of
approval.
      2.   The Director shall provide due notice to the applicant/owner of the
violation of any conditions of approval.
      3.   If the violations continue, the Director may order a public hearing
before the deciding body, in conformance with Chapters 8-6 and 8-9.
      4.   At the public hearing, the deciding body may, in whole or in part:
         a.   Affirm the approval;
         b.   Reverse the approval;
         c.   Modify the approval; or
         d.   Make or substitute any additional conditions that it determines
are warranted.
      5.   To act except to affirm the approval, the deciding body must find
there is a violation of the conditions of approval of an application within the
authority of the deciding body and one or more of the following:
         a.   The violation has caused or will cause detriment to the public
health, safety, or welfare.
         b.   The violation has created or will create undue adverse impact on
surrounding properties.
         c.   The violation has caused or will cause the approved use to be
served by inadequate public or private facilities.
         d.   The violation has impeded or will impede the normal development
of surrounding property.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)

8-9-5: HISTORIC PRESERVATION:
   A.   Purpose: The purpose of this Section is to promote the educational,
cultural, economic, and general welfare of the public of Ada County through the
identification, evaluation, designation, and protection of those buildings,
sites, areas, structures, and objects which reflect significant elements of the
County's, the state's, and the nation's historic, architectural,
archaeological, and cultural heritage.
   B.   Council Created:
      1.   There is hereby created a historic preservation council which shall
consist of members who shall be appointed by the Board. The number of members
shall be set by the bylaws of the council and shall be consistent with the
standards set for participation in the national park services' certified local
government program and Idaho Code Section 67-4601 et seq., as may be amended
and/or retitled in the future.
      2.   All members of the council shall have a demonstrated interest,
competence, or knowledge in history or historic preservation. The Board shall
endeavor to appoint at least two (2) members with professional training or
experience in the disciplines of architecture, history, architectural history,
urban planning, archaeology, engineering, law, or other historic preservation
related disciplines.
      3.   All appointments shall be made for three (3) year terms. Council
members may be reappointed to serve additional terms. Vacancies shall be filled
in the same manner as original appointments and the appointee shall serve for a
full term.
   C.   Organization And Administration:
      1.   The Council shall have the power to make whatever rules are
necessary for the execution of its duties as set forth in this Chapter. Rules
of procedure and bylaws adopted by the council shall be available for public
inspection. Changes to bylaws shall be approved by the Board after adoption by
the council.
      2.   The council shall elect a chairman and vice chairman from among the
council members. The chairman shall preside at meetings of the council. The
vice chairman shall, in the absence of the chairman, perform the duties of the
chairman.
      3.   All meetings of the council shall be open to the public and follow
the requirements of Idaho's open meeting laws. The council shall keep minutes
and other appropriate written records of its resolutions, proceedings, and
actions.
      4.   The council may recommend to the Board the employment of or the
contracting with other parties for the services of technical experts or other
persons, to assist the council in its functions.
   D.   Powers, Duties And Responsibilities: The council shall be advisory to
the Board and shall be authorized to:
      1.   Conduct a survey of local historic properties.
      2.   Recommend the acquisition, by the County, of fee simple and lesser
interests in historic properties, including adjacent or associated lands, by
purchase, bequest, or donation.
      3.   Recommend methods and procedures necessary to preserve, restore,
maintain and operate historic properties under the ownership or control of the
County.
      4.   Recommend that the lease, sale, or other transfer or disposition of
historic properties be made subject to rights of public access and other
covenants and in a manner that will preserve the property.
      5.   Draft and submit to the Board for approval, contracts with the state
or federal government, or any agency of either, or with any other organization.
      6.   Cooperate with the federal, state, and local governments in the
pursuance of the objectives of historic preservation.
      7.   Make recommendations and otherwise participate in the planning
processes undertaken by cities, the County, the state, or the federal
government and related agencies.
      8.   Recommend ordinances to the County and otherwise provide information
for the purposes of historic preservation in the County.
      9.   Promote and conduct educational and interpretive programs on
historic preservation and historic properties in the County.
      10.   Enter private property, buildings, or structures in the performance
of its official duties, but only with the express consent of the owner or
occupant thereof.
      11.   Review nominations of properties, within the County's jurisdiction,
to the National Register of Historic Places and provide comments to the state
historic preservation office.
      12.   Nominate properties within the County's jurisdiction to the
National Register of Historic Places.
      13.   Review requests for demolition of any structure fifty (50) years
old or older for historical significance prior to the issuance of a demolition
permit.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)

      10.   Subdivision of property.

***** CHAPTER 10
RULES OF INTERPRETATION AND DEFINITIONS *****
SECTION:
8-10-1:    Purpose And General Rules Of Interpretation
8-10-2:    Defined Terms
8-10-3:    Acronyms And Abbreviations
8-10-1: PURPOSE AND GENERAL RULES OF INTERPRETATION:
   A.   Purpose: This Chapter describes the general rules of interpretation and
provides definitions for those terms used in the Ada County Zoning Ordinance.
   B.   Language:
      1.   Terminology: When used in this Title, all words used in the present
tense shall include the future; words used in the singular number shall include
the plural number and the plural the singular, unless the natural construction
of the sentence indicates otherwise. The word "shall" is mandatory, and the
word "may" is permissive.
      2.   Number Of Days: Whenever a number of days is specified in this
Title, or in any permit, condition of approval, or notice issued or given as
provided in this Title, the number of days are construed as calendar days,
except that those time limits shall extend to the following working day when
the last of the specified number of days falls on a weekend or Ada County
holiday.
      3.   Section Headings: Section headings or captions are for reference
purposes only and shall not be used in the interpretation of this Title.
      4.   References: All references to state or federal laws and/or
regulations shall refer to such laws and/or regulations as they may be amended
over time.
   C.   Measurements:
      1.   Structure height is measured as the vertical distance from the
average contact ground level at the front wall of a building to the highest
point of the coping of a flat roof, the deck line of a mansard roof, or the
average height of the highest gable of a pitch or hip roof.
      2.   Linear distance is measured in a horizontal line. It is not measured
along an inclined surface or line. For uses that have a separation standard,
the distance is measured from the nearest customer entrance of the proposed use
to the nearest property line of the specified use. This measurement is
conducted in a radial fashion by the specified number of feet (e.g., 300 feet,
1,000 feet). Illumination levels are measured with a calibrated photoelectric
photometer or similar device capable of accurate measurement of light.
      3.   Noise levels are measured at the property line with a calibrated
noise meter or similar device capable of accurate measurement of sound. See
Figure 8-10-1-1 Noise Measurement.
   Figure 8-10-1-1 Noise Measurement
[https://export.amlegal.com/media/035b8d64e31d29757afadad2392dbd606a8eb6d9/
IMAGES/0-0-0-3541.png]
 
   D.   District Boundaries: Where uncertainty exists about the location of any
district boundary shown on the official zoning map, the following rules are
used to resolve the uncertainty:
      1.   Where a district boundary approximately follows a property line,
that property line is construed as the district boundary.
      2.   Where a district boundary approximately follows a street, alley, or
railroad line, that street, alley, centerline, or the extension of that line,
is construed as the district boundary. Where a street or alley is officially
vacated and that street or alley has not been given a zoning designation, the
land that was formerly in the vacated street or alley shall have the same
designation as the abutting property on either side of the centerline of the
vacated street or alley.
      3.   Where a district boundary approximately follows a watercourse, the
centerline of the watercourse is construed as that boundary. If a change
watercourse shoreline, the boundary is construed as moving with the actual
centerline.
      4.   Where a district boundary does not obviously coincide with any of
the above lines (property; street, alley, or railroad line; watercourse), or
where it is not designated by dimensions, it is located along nearest section,
a quarter section, or a sixteenth section line.
(Ord. 1002, 10-28-2025)
8-10-2: DEFINED TERMS:
ABANDONED: To cease or discontinue a use of activity for twelve (12) months
unless an active building permit has been issued.
ABUT OR ABUTTING: Having a common border with the subject property, which may
include public right of way.
ACCESS: Ingress/egress to a property, parcel, or lot.
ACCESSORY OFFICE: An accessory use involving any office related functions to a
primary use.
ACCESSORY OUTDOOR STORAGE: An accessory use involving the outdoor storage of
materials, supplies, and products to a primary use.
ACCESSORY POWER FACILITY: A wind facility or solar facility where electricity
is primarily produced for use on site with excess supplied to a power grid. The
generation capacity shall be one hundred (100) kilowatts or less.
ACCESSORY RETAIL SALES: The sale, distribution, presentation, demonstration, or
supply of goods to consumers through or at a retail store.
ACCESSORY STRUCTURE: A detached structure in a rural or residential base
district that is incidental and subordinate to the principal structure and is
located upon the same property. (Hallways, tunnels, breezeways, porticos, and
similar connections shall not constitute an attachment to the principal
permitted dwelling.) The term accessory structure shall include, but not be
limited to, the following: private garage, storage structure, workshop,
greenhouse, and/or a structure that houses a detached secondary dwelling. The
term shall not include additional structures for approved public, commercial,
or industrial uses.
ACCESSORY USE: A use that is incidental and subordinate to the principal or
approved conditional use and is conducted upon the same property. For the
purposes of this Title, temporary uses specified in Sections
8-4-73 and
8-6-29 of this Title shall be deemed accessory uses.
ADDITIONAL FARM DWELLING: A dwelling that complies with the requirements for a
"Dwelling, Additional Farm" in Chapter 8-4.
ADULT BOOTH: A separate enclosure within a structure featuring adult
entertainment or adult material. The term adult booth does not include a
restroom or a foyer through which any person can enter or exit the
establishment.
ADULT CABARET: An establishment that features adult entertainment.
ADULT ENTERTAINMENT: Material or performances distinguished or characterized by
an emphasis on matter depicting, describing, or relating to 'Specified Sexual
Activities' or 'Specified Anatomical Areas' for observation by its patrons or
limits the presentation of those materials to persons over eighteen (18) years
of age. This definition does not apply to a legitimate theatrical performance
where nudity is only incidental to the primary purpose of the performance. For
the purposes of this definition:
   1.   "Specified Sexual Activities" are defined as: a. human genitals in a
state of sexual stimulation or arousal; b. acts of human masturbation, sexual
intercourse, or sodomy; c. fondling or other erotic touching of human genitals,
pubic region, buttock, or female breast.
   2.   "Specified Anatomical Areas" are defined as: a. less than completely
and opaquely covered: 1. human genitals, pubic region, 2. buttock, and 3.
female breast below a point immediately above the top of the areola; and 4.
human male genitals in a discernibly turgid state, even if completely and
opaquely covered.
ADULT ENTERTAINMENT ESTABLISHMENT: A place where adult entertainment occurs,
where adult material is available, an adult cabaret, adult booth, adult
modeling or display establishment, adult motel, or adult theater.
ADULT MATERIAL: One or more of the following materials that have as their
primary or dominant theme matter depicting, illustrating, describing, or
relating to adult entertainment, regardless of whether it is new or used: 1.
books, magazines, periodicals or other printed matter; 2. photographs, films,
motion pictures, videocassettes, slides, or other visual representations; 3.
recordings or other audio matter.
   The term adult material shall also include instruments, novelties, devices,
or paraphernalia that are designed for use in connection with adult
entertainment.
ADULT MODELING OR DISPLAY ESTABLISHMENT: Any establishment whose employees
engage in adult entertainment or adult private modeling.
ADULT MOTEL: Any motel, hotel, boarding house, rooming house, or other place of
temporary lodging that includes the word "adult" or "erotic" in any name it
uses, or otherwise provides or advertises adult entertainment or adult
material.
ADULT PRIVATE MODELING: Modeling, posing, exhibition, display, or exposure by
an employee relating to adult entertainment before a nonemployee while the
nonemployee is in an area not accessible to all other persons in the
establishment, or while the nonemployee is in an area either totally or
partially screened or partitioned during such display from the view of all
persons outside the area. The term "private performance" is considered private
modeling.
ADULT THEATER: An establishment consisting of an enclosed structure, or a
portion or part of an enclosed structure, or an open-air area where a person
may view adult material or adult entertainment. Generally, the adult material
or adult entertainment is prerecorded material.
ADULT VIDEO OR BOOK STORE: An establishment that sells or rents adult material;
however, any establishment meeting all the following criteria shall not be
considered an adult video or bookstore:
   1.   The adult material is accessible only by employees.
   2.   The individual items of adult material offered for sale and/or rental
comprise less than ten percent (10%) of the individual items publicly displayed
at the establishment as stock in trade in the following categories: videos,
books, magazines, periodicals, other printed matter, slides, other visual
representations, recordings, and other audio matter.
   3.   The establishment does not use the following terms in advertisements or
other promotional activities relating to the adult materials: "XXX," "XX," "X,"
or any series of the letter "X" whether or not interspersed with other letters,
figures, or characters; "erotic" or deviations of that word; "adult
entertainment" or similar phrases; "sex" or "sexual acts" or similar phrases;
"nude" or "nudies" or similar phrases; or any other letters, words, or phrases
that promote the purchase or rental of adult material.
AGRICULTURAL LAND, PRIME: Land that contains class I, II, or III agricultural
soils as defined by the land capability classification assigned by the Natural
Resources Conservation Service of the United States Department of Agriculture.
AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE STAND: An establishment for the display and sale to the
general public of "produce" as defined in this Section, which produce has been
grown on the premises on a seasonal basis. No other commodities may be sold.
AGRICULTURAL SERVICE: An activity that provides support for agriculture and
forestry as classified by the U.S. Census Bureau "North American Industrial
Classification System." The term shall include agricultural service composting.
The use must serve a rural district with agricultural use.
AGRICULTURAL STRUCTURE: A structure on a "farm," excluding any dwelling or any
structure that shelters any personal items not directly needed for agricultural
uses.
AGRICULTURAL USE: Activities that take place on a "farm," as herein defined,
that are classified by the Ada County Assessor's Office tax categories of 010,
020, 030, 040, and/or 050. The application of fertilizer or process wastewater
at agronomic rates shall be deemed a component of the agricultural use.
AGRITAINMENT: Events and activities (such as corn mazes, hayrides, and petting
zoos, that allow for recreation, entertainment, and tourism in conjunction with
agriculture support and services) that are directly associated with an ongoing
agricultural use on-site.
AGRONOMIC RATE: The application of fertilizer or other crop supplements: a) at
rates whereby the nutrients are fully taken up by the crop or stored in the
soil, and b) in a manner that does not negatively impact the waters of the
state.
AIRCRAFT LANDING FIELD (PRIVATE): A privately owned area of land that is used
or intended for the landing and takeoff of aircraft, including the necessary
accessory structures or facilities for storing and maintenance of aircraft.
AIRPORT INFLUENCE AREAS: The areas surrounding the Boise air terminal that are
affected by significant aircraft noise and safety hazards, as set forth in
Section
8-2-24 of this Title.
AIRPORT: Any area of land or water which is used or intended for the landing
and taking off of aircraft, and any appurtenant areas which are used or
intended for use for airport buildings or other airport facilities or rights-
of-way. This includes all necessary runways, taxiways, aircraft storage and
tie-down areas, hangers, public terminal buildings and parking, helicopter
pads, support activities such as airport operations and air traffic control,
and other necessary buildings and open spaces. Includes dusting services. For
purposes of this definition, "aircraft" means a device that is used or intended
to be used for flight in the air, such as an airplane or helicopter.
ALIQUOT: The length of one side of a quarter-quarter section (1/16). The one-
sixteenth (1/16) section contains forty (40) acres, more or less.
ALTERNATIVE FUEL: A fuel that is used primarily to power combustion engines
that includes, but is not limited to, biodiesel, electricity, ethanol,
hydrogen, methanol, natural gas and propane.
AMATEUR RADIO ANTENNA: The supporting towers and antenna structure necessary
for broadcast from a radio communication service for the purpose of self-
training, intercommunication, and technical investigation carried out by
amateurs, that is, duly authorized persons interested in radio technique solely
with a personal aim and without commercial interest.
AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT: 42 U.S.C. Chapter 126 and 28 CFR Part 36 (Part
36 Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Public Accommodations and
Commercial Facilities), and Standards and Specifications, 2010 ADA Standards
for Accessible Design (United States Department of Justice, September 15,
2010), Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accessibility Guidelines for
Buildings and Facilities.
AMUSEMENT OR RECREATION, INDOOR: An establishment engaged in providing
amusement, recreation, or entertainment. Indoor amusement or recreation
facility shall include, but not be limited to, pool hall, billiard parlor,
theater, health club, spa, fitness facility, nightclub, or skating rink.
AMUSEMENT OR RECREATION, OUTDOOR: An establishment engaged in providing
amusement, recreation, or entertainment. Outdoor amusement or recreation
facility shall include, but not be limited to, amusement park, miniature golf,
golf driving range (that is not accessory to a golf course), drive-in theater,
tennis court, football, soccer, rugby, or hockey field, skatepark, or swimming
pool.
ANIMAL FEEDING OPERATION (AFO): A "livestock confinement facility," as herein
defined, with more than three hundred (300) animal units, and where the animal
confinement areas do not sustain crops, vegetation, forage growth, or
postharvest residues in the normal growing season as generally described in 40
CFR (code of Federal Regulations) 122.23(b)(1). Two (2) or more abutting AFOs
under common ownership shall be considered a single AFO. Two (2) or more AFOs
that are operated as a single facility shall be considered a single AFO if it
is determined by the Director that they significantly link operations
including, but not limited to, shared storage or treatment systems or shared
equipment.
ANIMAL UNIT: A unit of measurement for livestock confinement facilities
calculated by adding the following numbers: the combined weight of all dairy
cattle divided by one thousand three hundred fifty (1,350); plus the combined
weight of all other cattle divided by one thousand four hundred (1,400); plus
the combined weight of all swine divided by six hundred (600); plus the
combined weight of all sheep divided by one thousand two hundred fifty (1,250);
plus the combined weight of all goats divided by one thousand (1,000); plus the
combined weight of all horses divided by one thousand five hundred (1,500);
plus the combined weight of all chickens divided by three hundred fifty (350);
plus the combined weight of all turkeys divided by five hundred (500); plus the
combined weight of all ducks divided by two hundred (200). Where an AU is not
specifically defined in this Title for an animal, an appropriate AU shall be
determined by the Director with advice from the Idaho department of
agriculture.
ANTENNA: Any system of wires, poles, rods, reflecting discs, or similar devices
used for the collection, transmission, radiation, or reception of
electromagnetic waves, external to or attached to the exterior of any
structure. This includes both directional antennas, such as panels and
microwave dishes, and omnidirectional antennas, such as whips and satellite
dishes, but not including satellite earth stations.
ANTENNA HUB SITE: An area containing one or more unmanned equipment structures
sited to serve telecommunications antennas. An antenna hub site may be located
on the same lot as the antennas served or located on a lot that does not
contain the antennas served.
ANTENNA SUPPORT STRUCTURE: A self-supporting or bracketed ground-mounted pole
sixty (60) feet or less in height that is accessory to and used to support one
or more telecommunications antennas and no more than one related unmanned
equipment structure.
APARTMENT: A room or suite of rooms in a multi-family development for sale,
rent, lease, let, or hire to be used as a single dwelling.
APPEAL: A request for a review of any decision by the Ada County Director or
the Planning and Zoning Commission in applying the Ada County Zoning Ordinance.
APPELLANT: A party of record or other person who is entitled by law to appeal
and who initiates an appeal.
APPLICANT: The person or entity seeking an approval of an application required
by this Title, including a decision from the Director or the Board, or a
decision or recommendation from the Commission. The "applicant" includes the
owner of the property subject to an application.
APPLICATION: The document utilized by a person seeking approval for an act
under this Title.
APPROVED USE: A use that has been approved.
AREA OF IMPACT: Those unincorporated areas of Ada County surrounding each
incorporated city as identified in Title 9 of this code, in accord with Idaho
Code Section 67-6526.
ASPHALT OR CONCRETE READY-MIX PLANT: A central proportioning and mixing plant
for the production of an aggregate product such as asphalt or concrete.
AUCTION: Premises on which merchandise is stored on a temporary basis to be
sold through an on-site auction.
AUTOMOBILE WRECKING YARD: Any area, lot, land, or parcel where more than two
(2) motor vehicles without current registration or more than two (2) inoperable
or dismantled motor vehicles that are not in operating condition (or parts
thereof) are: a) standing more than thirty (30) days, b) dismantled, or c)
stored. The following uses are excluded from this definition: agricultural
equipment on a "farm" as herein defined, automotive hobby as set forth in
Section 8-4-8 of this Title, and vehicles stored or dismantled within a
completely enclosed structure.
AUTOMOTIVE, HOBBY: An accessory use involving the restoration, maintenance,
and/or preservation of not more than two (2) vehicles at any one time.
BAR: A structure used primarily for the sale or dispensing of liquor by the
drink or glass, but not including restaurants where the principal business is
serving food.
BARRIER: A vertical element including, but not limited to, a fence, wall,
structure, or a combination thereof, that completely surrounds an area and
controls access to such area.
BASE DISTRICT: The zone district classification, listed in Section
8-2-3 of this Title, in effect on any given property.
BEACON: Any light with one or more beams directed into the atmosphere or
directed at one or more points not on the same property as the light source;
also, any light with one or more beams that rotate or move.
BED AND BREAKFAST ESTABLISHMENT: An owner-occupied dwelling providing overnight
accommodations and breakfast food service for no more than ten (10) occupants,
including the owner and owner's family.
BERM: A raised landform designed to provide visual interest, screen undesirable
views, and/or decrease noise.
BICYCLE PARKING FACILITIES: Any area or necessary equipment to store bicycles
on a short- or long-term basis. Bicycle parking facilities include spaces,
racks, lockers, cages, and secured parking locations.
BILLBOARD: A permanent, off-premises sign or sign structure on which a person
places copy on a poster or panel mounted on a pole or metal structure.
Typically, a billboard has one of the following configurations: 1. wood posts
or pole supports with dimensional lumber as the secondary support (A-frame)
with a wood or metal catwalk with display panels, 2. steel A-frame constructed
with angle iron or steel supports with metal framing, catwalk, with display
panels, 3. multi-mast structure constructed with steel poles, I-beam, or
equivalent member as the primary support, with a catwalk, and display panels,
or 4. monopole structure constructed with tubular steel support, tubular steel
framing, metal catwalk, and display panels with a concrete foundation.
BIOMASS FACILITY: A type of power facility that converts the energy stored in
renewable organic material into electricity. Renewable organic materials used
in the conversion process include, but are not limited to, wood, crops, animal
waste, garbage, landfill gas, biogas, and alcohol fuels.
BLANKETING: A term applicable to signs or sign structures where the partial or
complete shutting off of the face of one sign by another sign.
BLOCK: A piece of land or group of lots within a platted subdivision.
BOARD: Board of Ada County Commissioners.
BOARDING HOUSE: An establishment with individual rooms where meals and lodging
are provided for, with or without compensation, to more than two (2) but not
more than ten (10) persons. A boarding house shall include, but not be limited
to, a rooming house, shelter, convent, monastery, dormitory, fraternity house,
sorority house, or any group of individuals whose association is temporary or
seasonal in nature. Hotels, motels, multi-family developments, and bed and
breakfast establishments are not considered boarding houses.
BREWERY: An establishment that brews thirty thousand (30,000) barrels of beer
or more annually and as defined by Idaho Code Section 23-1003. The use may
include the ancillary sale or dispensing of beer or malt liquor by the drink or
glass.
BREWPUB or DISTILLERY: A brewpub is an establishment that brews less than
thirty thousand (30,000) barrels of beer annually and as defined by Idaho Code
Section 23-1003. A distillery is an establishment that produces spirits, as
defined by Idaho Code Section 23-105. A brewery or distillery may include a
restaurant, sale of alcoholic beverages by the drink or glass, and/or retail
sale of the products of the brewery or distillery.
BUFFER: A combination of physical space and vertical elements, including, but
not limited to, plants, berms, fences, and/or walls that separate and screen
incompatible land uses from one another.
BUILDING AREA: This is expressed as the maximum per building, in gross floor
area (gfa). The building area is determined using the methodology established
in the Ada County Building Code.
BUILDING ENVELOPE: The area on a property exclusive of required yards and
unbuildable areas (including, but not limited to, slopes in excess of twenty-
five percent (25%) and areas within a designated floodway).
BUILDING FACE: Where sign size is prescribed as a percent of building face
area, the "building face area" is a continuous portion of a building facade, as
viewed by a person approaching the building from the public right-of-way,
consisting of a plane surface including the parapet wall but excluding any
appurtenances, such as columns, pilasters, canopies, marquees, showcases, or
decorations.
BUILDING HEIGHT: Building height is measured as the vertical distance from the
average ground level at the front wall of a building to the highest point of
the coping of a flat roof, the deck line of a mansard roof, or the average
height of the highest gable of a pitch or hip roof.
BUILDING MARKER: Any sign indicating the name of a structure, a date, or other
incidental information about its construction cut into a masonry surface or
made of bronze or other permanent material.
BUILDING OFFICIAL: The officer or other designated authority charged with the
administration and enforcement of the Ada County Building Code, or the building
official's duly authorized representative.
CALENDAR DAY: Sunday through Saturday, including all holidays.
CALIPER: A measurement of the diameter of the trunk of a deciduous tree. The
caliper of the trunk shall be measured six inches (6") above the ground for all
trees up to and including four-inch (4") caliper size, and twelve inches (12")
above the ground for larger sizes.
CAMPGROUND: An area or tract of land that accommodates one or more temporary
residential uses, including, but not limited to, cabins, tents, campers, travel
trailers, motor homes, and/or recreational vehicles.
CAPITAL IMPROVEMENTS PROGRAM (CIP): A plan that describes when urban public
facilities will be built, how much they will cost, and the source of funding. A
CIP usually covers a period of between three (3) and ten (10) years.
CAR WASH: An establishment or area that provides facilities for washing and
cleaning vehicles, which may use production line methods with a conveyor,
blower, or other mechanical devices, and that may employ some hand labor. The
facility may include vacuums and drying areas as accessory uses.
CARETAKER DWELLING: See Dwelling, Caretaker.
CELL TOWER HEIGHT: The distance from the finished grade at the tower base to
the highest point of the tower, plus twenty feet (20') to accommodate
additional antenna colocation.
CEMETERY: A place dedicated to, used and intended to be used for, the permanent
interment of the human dead, and may include a burial plot for earth
interments, a mausoleum for vault or crypt interments, a crematory, or a
crematory and columbarium for cinerary interments, or a combination of one or
more of the above.
CENTRALIZED POWER FACILITY: A geothermal, solar, biomass, or hydroelectric
power facility where electricity is produced with a capacity greater than one
hundred (100) kilowatts and is transmitted to other locations for consumption.
This includes all buildings and structures on the site that are used to
generate power, including power generators, equipment, and other structures
that are located on-site.
CHILDREN'S TREATMENT FACILITY: An establishment, or portion thereof, that: a)
provides permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and
sanitation for more than eight (8) juveniles under eighteen (18) years old, and
b) provides treatment for substance abuse, mental illness, emotional
disturbance, developmental disability, mental retardation, or juveniles who
have been identified by the judicial system as requiring treatment, therapy,
rehabilitation, or supervision. For purposes of this Title, this definition
shall include group foster homes with more than thirteen (13) juveniles.
CLEAR VISION TRIANGLE: An area at the intersection of two (2) streets that is
clear of sight obstructions to motorists (see Figures 10-2-1a and 10-2-1b).

CLIENT: For purposes of the day care (day care center; day care home, family;
and day care facility, group) and group foster home definitions, a "client" is
a person who receives direct care from providers at a day care facility, or a
group foster home.
CLINIC (DENTAL OR MEDICAL): A facility (including any room, studio, clinic,
suite, or building) where individuals licensed in the State practice medicine,
osteopathy, dentistry, chiropractic, podiatry, physical therapy, psychiatry,
clinical psychology, or other health-related professions on an out-patient
basis. This does not include a hospital, veterinary service, or animal
hospital.
COLLOCATION: The use of a single structure to support more than one wireless
telecommunication service provider's equipment, or the mounting of an antenna
to a preexisting structure.
COMMERCIAL VEHICLE: Any vehicle defined by Idaho Code Section 49-123.
COMMISSION: The Planning and Zoning Commission of Ada County, Idaho.
COMPOSTING FACILITY: A facility for the production of compost intended for use
on premises other than where the compost is produced. This does not include
wood chipping activities that result wood bark sales on-and-off site, as this
is not a fertilizer.
COMPREHENSIVE PLAN: The duly adopted comprehensive plan for a political
subdivision of the state of Idaho pursuant to the "Local Land Use Planning
Act," Idaho Code Section 67-6501 et seq., as amended.
CONDITIONAL USE: A use that, owing to some special characteristics, attendant
to its operation or installation (for example, potential danger, hours of
operation, or noise), is permitted in a district only subject to approval by
the Planning and Zoning Commission and subject to special requirements as
enabled by Idaho Code Section 67-6512.
CONDOMINIUM: An estate in real property as defined in Idaho Code Section 55-
101B that is not a subdivision.
CONFINEMENT AREAS: Any area or structure where livestock and/or poultry are
stabled, confined, gathered, fed, maintained, and/or milked and where such
areas do not sustain crops, vegetation, forage growth, or postharvest residues
in the normal growing season.
CONSERVATION EASEMENT: A nonpossessory interest of a holder in real property
imposing limitations or affirmative obligations, the purposes of which include
retaining or protecting natural, scenic, or open space values of real property,
assuring its availability for agricultural, forest, recreational, or open space
use, protecting natural resources, maintaining or enhancing air or water
quality, or preserving the historical, architectural, archaeological, or
cultural aspects of real property.
CONSOLIDATION: The process of combining two parcels of land into one. This is
not a subdivision process.
CONTIGUOUS PARCELS: Un-platted parcels held in one ownership that abut each
other at a common boundary. See also Section
8-3-2D of this Title.
CONTINUING CARE FACILITY: A building or structure used for any of the
following:
   Congregate Living Facility: An establishment that provides independent
living affiliated with or located near health care facilities. This also
includes children's treatment facilities.
   Adult Assisted Living: An establishment for people who cannot live
independently and who need assistance with daily chores and housekeeping.
   Nursing Home: An establishment for individuals who require specialized
nursing care on a regular basis but who do not need to be hospitalized. This
use also includes residential care facilities and adult respite health care
centers.
   Skilled Nursing Facility: An establishment that provides permanent
provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation and that
provides healthcare needs to more than eight (8) individuals who, at a minimum,
require: a) inpatient care and services for twenty-four (24) or more
consecutive hours for unstable chronic health problems, b) daily professional
nursing supervision and licensed nursing care on a twenty-four (24) hour basis,
and c) restorative, rehabilitative care and assistance in meeting daily living
needs. Medical supervision may be necessary on a regular, but not daily, basis.
A skilled nursing facility shall include, but not be limited to: convalescent
home, intermediate care, and subacute care.
   Residential Care Facility: An establishment that provides permanent
provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation and that
provides twenty-four (24) hour nonmedical care for more than eight (8)
individuals who need personal care or assistance and supervision. A residential
care facility shall include, but not be limited to, assisted living facility,
retirement home, and respite care.
CONTINUOUS SERVICE DRIVE: A privately owned and maintained continuous drive
providing for ingress and egress to a public road, internal vehicle
circulation, and emergency access in a multi-family, commercial or industrial
development.
CONTRACTOR: A person who agrees to furnish materials or perform services at a
specified price, especially for construction. The term contractor shall
include, but not be limited to, building, landscaping, electrical, plumbing,
heating, or air conditioning contractors.
CONTRACTOR YARD: Any area of land used by a contractor for storage,
maintenance, or processing incidental to the business of building, hauling,
excavation, demolition, or similar activity and including any area of land used
for the incidental repair of machinery used for any of the above listed
activities.
COUNTY: Ada County, Idaho.
COUNTY CODE: The Ada County, Idaho, Code of Ordinances. This term may also be
referred to as "Code."
COUNTY ENGINEER: That licensed in the state of Idaho professional engineer
appointed by the Board who is responsible for all engineering matters for Ada
County.
COUNTY SURVEYOR: That licensed in the state of Idaho professional land surveyor
appointed by the Board to check plats and monuments for compliance with
platting and surveying laws, provide for surveying monument records, and make
such surveys, descriptions, maps, and plats as ordered by the Board.
COVERAGE: The area of a property occupied by the footprint of all structures.
CREMATORY: A facility used primarily for human funeral services, which may or
may not include facilities on the premises for embalming and performing of
autopsies or other surgical procedures. This facility conducts cremation or
incineration for deceased individuals.
CUTOFF ANGLE: The angle formed by a line drawn from the direction of light rays
at the light source and a line perpendicular to the ground from the light
source, above which the light is emitted.
DAIRY: An operation whose principal function is the production of milk,
including the barn, processing facility, or feeding area where dairy animals
are kept, raised, or fed.
DANGEROUS OR PROTECTED ANIMAL: Any species for which the state or federal
government has established specific regulations regarding such animal
including, but not limited to, big cats, bears, raptors, large reptiles, and
other wildlife. The term shall not include any species commonly recognized as
domestic pets.
DANGEROUS OR PROTECTED ANIMAL FACILITY: A building, structure, or enclosure
where dangerous or protected animals are maintained, harbored, possessed,
trained, bred, boarded, or cared for.
DAY-NIGHT AVERAGE SOUND LEVEL (DNL): The twenty four (24) hour average sound
level, in decibels, for the period from midnight to midnight, obtained after
the addition of ten decibels to sound levels for the periods between midnight
and seven o'clock (7:00) A.M., and between ten o'clock (10:00) P.M., and
midnight, local time. The symbol for DNL is Ldn. (Source: 14 C.F.R. § 150.7.)
DAY CARE CENTER: A place or facility providing day care for compensation for
thirteen (13) or more clients. Day camps, day programs and religious schools
held for more than two (2) weeks during a calendar year or held more often than
once a week, are considered day care centers. The provision of occasional care
exclusively for clients of parents who are simultaneously in the same building
is not considered a day care center.
DAY CARE FACILITY, GROUP: A home, place or facility providing care and
supervision for compensation for part of a day, for seven (7) to twelve (12)
clients not related by blood or marriage to the person(s) providing the care,
in a place other than the clients' own home. The occasional care of clients by
a person not ordinarily in the business of childcare, and the provision of care
for clients of only one immediate family in addition to the person's own
children are not considered group day care facilities.
DAY CARE HOME, FAMILY: A home, place, or facility providing care and
supervision for compensation for part of a day, for six (6) or fewer clients
not related by blood or marriage to the person providing the care, in a place
other than the clients' own home. The occasional care of clients by a person
not ordinarily in the business of childcare, and the provision of care for
clients of only one immediate family in addition to the person's own children
are not considered family day care homes.
dBA: The A-weighted scale for measuring sound in decibels; weighs or reduces
the effects of low and high frequencies in order to simulate human hearing.
DECISION MAKING BODY: The Director, Commission, or Board, as set forth in
Chapter 8-9 of this Title. The decision-making bodies are identified as the
bodies making a "decision" in Section
8-6-2,
Table 8-6-2-1.
DEDICATION: The setting apart of land or interests in land for public use,
charitable, religious, or educational purposes.
DENSITY: The ratio of the total number of dwelling units within a development
divided by the total area. Should that number be a fraction, it shall be
rounded to the nearest whole number.
DENSITY, NET: The ratio of the total number of dwelling units within a
development divided by the area devoted to residential uses (excluding roadways
and/or required dedicated open space). Should that number be a fraction, it
shall be rounded to the nearest whole number.
DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT: A written agreement as a condition of zoning ordinance
map amendment between the Board and an owner concerning the use or development
of a property in accord with Idaho Code Section 67-6511A and Section 8-6-17 of
this Title.
DEVELOPMENT: Any construction or installation of a structure, or any change in
use of a structure, or any change in the use, character, or appearance of land.
DIRECTOR: The Director of the Ada County Development Services Department or an
authorized representative.
DISTRIBUTED POWER FACILITY: A wind or solar power facility where electricity is
primarily produced for use on site with excess supplied to a power grid. The
generation capacity shall be one hundred (100) kilowatts or less.
DISTRIBUTED POWER FACILITY, SOLAR ROOFTOP: A distributed power facility that
converts solar energy into electrical energy, and that is mounted on the
rooftop of a building.
DISTRIBUTED POWER FACILITY, WIND FREESTANDING TOWER: A wind or solar power
facility where electricity is primarily produced for use on site with excess
supplied to a power grid. The generation capacity shall be one hundred (100)
kilowatts or less.
DISTRIBUTED POWER FACILITY, WIND ROOFTOP: A distributed power facility that
converts wind energy into electrical energy, and that is mounted on the rooftop
of a building.
dNL: See "Day-night average sound level" above.
DOMESTIC PET: An animal kept for enjoyment and companionship that is housed
primarily inside a dwelling.
DRIVE AISLE: Provides access to off-street parking spaces. In some instances, a
continuous service drive may also double as the drive aisle.
DRIVE-UP ESTABLISHMENT : An establishment with drive-up window service.
DRIVE-UP WINDOW: Any portion of a structure or structure from which business is
transacted, or is capable of being transacted, directly with customers located
in a motor vehicle.
DRIVE-UP WINDOW SERVICE: An establishment providing a "drive-up window" as
herein defined. The term drive-up window service shall include, but not be
limited to, providing food or beverage service, and/or bank service. The term
drive-up window service shall not include "gasoline, diesel, or alternative
fuel sales facility" or "car wash" as herein defined.
DRUG AND ALCOHOL TREATMENT FACILITY: An establishment, or portion that: a)
provides permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and
sanitation, and b) provides a treatment program for adult patients (eighteen
(18) years and older) with a drug and/or alcohol use problem. This definition
shall include a detoxification facility, inpatient facility, residential
facility, clinic, and outpatient facility as they relate to drug and alcohol
treatment.
   Figure 8-10-2-3
